{"self_assessment": "Impact
I chose the animal and the design. I proposed a fish with a nose start, split top and bottom lines, and a rounded tail. I put it on the scratch pad as numbered strokes within the first 30 seconds, so everyone could start building at once. The fish was chosen because its outline reads clearly without any interior detail. The finished run connected all 126 dominoes from the start, and the judge was given a recognizable fish outline.

Execution
I sketched the full plan on the pad before any dominoes went down. Stroke 1 laid the start at the nose, and both lines left it in the same direction. The tail was drawn with rounded joins so the fall could carry through. During the build I inspected the joints and the right side at about 2:00, 3:00, 3:30 and 4:15, and each time confirmed the whole run was still connected from the nose. I called for hands off once the fish was complete, which reduced the risk of a late bump before the push.

Collaboration
I gave each person a clear stroke to own, so there was no overlap or waiting. I gave regular status updates to the table and answered Leo's concern about the tail pinch directly. I asked Leo and Priya where they wanted help and then left their strokes to them, rather than crowding the same stretch of table.

Leadership
I set the direction in the first minute, assigned the roles, and kept the table focused on one plan with no rework. I kept the team informed on the state of the run. I also made the call to stop adding to the fish once it was complete, which kept the table steady until the push.", "my_share_percent": 30}
